title: California's 40th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 40th Congressional District features two Republican incumbents — Ken Calvert, who currently represents the 41st District, and Young Kim, who currently represents the 40th District — after Proposition 50, a 2025 redistricting amendment, merged their constituencies into one seat. The June 2, 2026 top-two primary resulted in both Republicans advancing, locking out multiple Democratic candidates such as Esther Kim-Varet, Joe Kerr, and Lisa Ramirez. The newly drawn district spans parts of Orange and Riverside counties and is rated Solid/Likely Republican by the Cook Political Report. This member-versus-member contest will determine which incumbent returns to Congress in a race that has drawn national attention due to its implications for the battle over the House majority.
polling_note: No nonpartisan general election polls were found for the Calvert vs. Kim matchup. An internal campaign poll commissioned by Young Kim's campaign (Public Opinion Strategies, January 2026) focused on primary voters and is not a neutral general election survey.

candidates.name: Ken Calvert
candidates.summary: Ken Calvert is a Republican U.S. Representative first elected in 1992, currently representing California's 41st Congressional District. He is a lifelong resident of Riverside County, a former small business owner in the restaurant and real estate industries, and chairs the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense. Calvert is running on his record of conservative leadership and constituent service, emphasizing his work on E-Verify, transportation funding, and water projects.

candidates.name: Young Kim
candidates.summary: Young Kim is a Republican U.S. Representative first elected in 2020, currently representing California's 40th Congressional District. Born in South Korea, she immigrated to the U.S. and earned a BBA from USC, later working as a financial analyst, small business owner, and longtime staffer for Rep. Ed Royce. She previously served one term in the California State Assembly (2014–2016). Kim emphasizes her America First agenda, bipartisanship record, and work on the House Foreign Affairs and Financial Services Committees.

forecast.rationale: This is a same-party Republican-versus-Republican general election under California's top-two system, after Proposition 50 redistricting merged the old 40th (Young Kim) and 41st (Ken Calvert) districts. No nonpartisan general-election polling exists for the Calvert-Kim matchup; the only known poll is an internal primary survey commissioned by Kim's campaign, which is not a neutral indicator. The district is rated Solid/Likely Republican by Cook, ensuring the seat stays Republican regardless of outcome. Young Kim holds a slight informational edge as the current 40th District incumbent whose constituents form the core of the new district, but Ken Calvert brings decades of seniority, the chairmanship of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense, and deep roots in Riverside County. With no neutral polling and two well-funded, established incumbents, the race is highly uncertain. The 'other' rating reflects that this is not a standard Democratic-vs-Republican contest.
